title: Launch Helmsman timetable and fallout scenario notes (Apr 2026) - draft
content:
Summary:

This is a working notebook for the upcoming April micro-release. It bundles a time-aware operator timetable, a small matrix of likely fallout scenarios with concrete mitigations, and a first-pass set of release notes for product and infra audiences. The aim: give a single reference for shift leads (helmsman), the signal lead, and the engineering steward during the 72-hour launch window.

Top-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Keep 95th percentile token latency under 220ms for hosted tier A.
- Avoid cross-region dependency spikes (S3/GCS proxy).
- Validate canary regressions on the prompt-regression suite within 60 minutes of rollout start.

Helmsman roles and quick responsibilities:
- Helmsman (primary on-call): own go/no-go decisions, notify SRE & product, initiate rollback if latency or error signals cross thresholds.
- Signal lead: monitor telemetry, validate experiment fences, annotate incidents in the release docket.
- Engineering steward: triage PRs that surface during the window, gate hotfixes to ship with helmsman approval.

Hour-by-hour compact timetable (Launch day = D):
- D-2: Final smoke run in staging; export last-night telemetry snapshot to /tmp/release-snapshot; confirm alerts w/ SRE.
- D-1 09:00: Dry-run cutover on a 5% internal canary. Helmsman checks: latency, OOMs, KV cache hit rate.
- D 08:00: Helmsman briefing (15m) — confirm rollback plan, comm channel, on-call roster.
- D 09:00: Kickoff — shift signal to 5% production traffic, enable canary gating rules.
- D 09:30: Telemetry pass #1 (30m): compare prompt-regression pass/fail, token distributions, and prefix cache metrics.
- D 10:30: If clear, move to 30% for 45m. Otherwise, hold or roll back per gating matrix.
- D 11:30: Final ramp decision (helmsman) — full roll to 100% or stepback to safe-tier variant.
- D+1 12:00: Retrospective quick notes and ops log upload.

Telemetry anchors & primary signals to watch:
- Token latency: p50/p95/p99 and change rate vs baseline.
- Error rate: 5xx and model-inference error spikes.
- KV cache hit rate and cold-cache latency.
- GPU memory growth patterns (unexpected linear increases).
- Backend storage latency for artifacts (model shims, embeddings cache).

Fallout scenarios (likeliest) and mitigations:
1) Short-term latency spike at canary (p95 jumps 60%):
   - Immediate action: Helmsman drops to previous model variant and pins canary traffic to stable pool.
   - Notes: Start lightweight profiler on affected shard (record 60s). Open JIRA with tag JIRA-RELEASE-402-latency.
2) KV cache warmup fails (hit rate < 30% for 20m):
   - Action: switch to reduced-batch mode for inference, temporarily enable prefix work-cache bypass. Ask infra to increase burst capacity if queue grows.
3) OOM on a dedicated node type during rollout:
   - Action: cordon node, drain, allow autoscale to replace. If replacement fails, fall back to quantized variant for affected region. Notify customer-success for impacted tenants.
4) Unexpected model output regression (functional correctness on eval set):
   - Action: immediate canary pause, rollback to previous model version, trigger eval-run against the canonical prompt set. Create regression-ticket and schedule triage with Applied ML.

Quick checklist for shift handoff (pre-launch):
- Confirm on-call roster posted to #launch-helmsman.
- Ensure dashboard tabs for latency, error-rate, cache-hitrate open and bookmarked.
- Verify rollback artifacts are tagged and accessible (S3 path included in Jira ticket).
- Confirm communication templates for customer-status and internal incident.

Draft release notes (audience: product + infra) — to be edited for tone:
- Feature: Rolling canary support for model-variant mix to reduce cold-start effects.
- Improvement: Telemetry sampling increased for low-traffic routes to surface prefix-cache regressions faster.
- Fix: Corrected a throttling misestimate that caused request queueing under burst scenarios (affects dedicated pools only).
- Known issues: Some legacy embedding keys may show slightly different numeric scale after the quantized fallback; evaluations show no user-visible regression but signal team is monitoring.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Do we want a forced readout to customer-success for any tenant whose SLA is within 1% of breach during rollout? (ask @Aisha)
- Final decision on whether to enable aggressive autoscale for GPU_p3x2 in us-west-2 — cost vs safety tradeoff.
- Should we pre-seed KV prefix caches for top 200 production prompts (script exists but not run in last 7 days)?

Cross-links and quick refs:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/inference/telemetry-catalog (instrumentation spec)
- Jira: JIRA-RELEASE-402 (release ticket), JIRA-INT-88 (canary gating rules)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987 (canary rollback helper)
- Slack: #launch-helmsman (primary comms), #infra-surge (backstop)

Notes to self (Marcus):
- Keep the initial canary small and watch the embedding cache hits carefully — I saw a small drift in staging yesterday.
- Remind Priya to snapshot eval results pre-D so we have a reference.

Appendix: quick decision ladder (for helmsman) — use as shorthand during noisy windows:
- If p95 > 250ms or 5xx > 0.5% for > 5m: pause ramp and evaluate.
- If memory growth > 10% over baseline for 15m: cordon and revert variant.
- If functional regression flagged by regression-suite: immediate rollback and tag ML lead.

End of draft — please annotate inline or drop quick comments in the linked Confluence page.
